title: Vulkan from Zero
description: An interactive, visual Vulkan course for graphics people: every object, frame and barrier you can see and step through, with Rust (ash) and C++ (Vulkan-Hpp) code.

modules.title: Foundations
modules.summary: What a GPU is, how a program gets work onto it, why Vulkan is explicit, and the map of every Vulkan object.

lessons.title: What a GPU is
lessons.summary: Thousands of small cores, its own memory, and why it is fast at pixels and slow at decisions.

lessons.title: How a program talks to the GPU
lessons.summary: Application, driver, command buffers and queues: the path every draw call takes.

lessons.title: Why Vulkan exists
lessons.summary: OpenGL's hidden state machine versus Vulkan's explicit objects, and what you pay and get for it.

lessons.title: The map of Vulkan objects
lessons.summary: Every object of a Vulkan program on one map: who creates whom, and in what order.

modules.title: Instance
modules.summary: Install the tools, create the first Vulkan object and turn on the validation layers that will catch our mistakes.

lessons.title: Toolchain: SDK, Rust and C++ projects
lessons.summary: Vulkan SDK, vulkaninfo, vkconfig, and the two example projects: Rust with ash, C++ with Vulkan-Hpp.

lessons.title: The loader and VkInstance
lessons.summary: How the Vulkan loader finds drivers, and what an instance, layers and extensions are.

lessons.title: Validation layers and the debug messenger
lessons.summary: Layers that check every call against the spec, and how their messages reach our code.

modules.title: Devices and queues
modules.summary: Pick a GPU, learn what it can do, find its engines (queue families) and open a logical device with queues.

lessons.title: Physical devices: properties, features, limits
lessons.summary: Enumerating GPUs and reading what each one is and can do.

lessons.title: Queue families: the GPU's engines
lessons.summary: Graphics, compute, transfer: how queue families relate to the hardware engines inside the GPU.

lessons.title: Logical device and queues
lessons.summary: Opening a VkDevice with the features and queues we chose, and getting VkQueue handles.

modules.title: Presentation
modules.summary: Open a window, connect Vulkan to it through a surface, and build the swapchain: the ring of images the screen shows in turn.

lessons.title: A window and its surface
lessons.summary: Vulkan knows no windows: the WSI extensions, VkSurfaceKHR, and asking the GPU what it can show in our window.

lessons.title: The swapchain and present modes
lessons.summary: A ring of images owned by the presentation engine: format, present mode, size and image count.

lessons.title: Images and image views
lessons.summary: What a VkImage is, and why rendering and shaders look at images through VkImageView.

modules.title: The graphics pipeline
modules.summary: Shaders in Slang compiled to SPIR-V, the stages of the graphics pipeline, its layout, and rendering without render passes.

lessons.title: Shaders, Slang and SPIR-V
lessons.summary: From shader source to SPIR-V to a VkShaderModule: Vulkan's one binary shader format and how our triangle shader gets there.

lessons.title: The graphics pipeline object
lessons.summary: Every stage from vertex input to color blending baked into one VkPipeline, and the state left dynamic.

lessons.title: The pipeline layout
lessons.summary: The declaration of every resource a pipeline's shaders may read: descriptor set layouts and push constant ranges.

lessons.title: Dynamic rendering
lessons.summary: Rendering into image views named at record time: attachments, load and store operations, and what replaced VkRenderPass.

modules.title: Commands and the first triangle
modules.summary: Record commands into a command buffer, submit it to a queue, and put the first triangle on the screen.

lessons.title: Command pools and command buffers
lessons.summary: Where command buffers come from, what recording means, and how a submission reaches the queue.

lessons.title: The first triangle
lessons.summary: One frame end to end: wait, acquire, record, submit, present, with a fence, semaphores and two layout transitions.

modules.title: Synchronization
modules.summary: Who waits for whom: fences, semaphores and barriers, several frames in flight, timeline semaphores, and rebuilding the swapchain when the window changes.

lessons.title: Fences and semaphores
lessons.summary: The three tools that order GPU work - fence, semaphore, barrier - what each one connects, and how they relate to CPU threads and locks.

lessons.title: Frames in flight
lessons.summary: Let the CPU record the next frame while the GPU renders this one: per-frame resources, fence slots, and what it measurably buys.

lessons.title: Pipeline barriers and image layouts
lessons.summary: Execution and memory dependencies, stage and access masks, availability and visibility, and layout transitions, on a render-then-blit frame.

lessons.title: Timeline semaphores
lessons.summary: One 64-bit counter that only grows replaces a fence per frame; why acquire and present still need binary semaphores.

lessons.title: Swapchain recreation
lessons.summary: Resizing and minimizing the window: OUT_OF_DATE and SUBOPTIMAL, oldSwapchain, and knowing when the old swapchain is free - present fences or vkDeviceWaitIdle.

modules.title: Resources and memory
modules.summary: Where the bytes of a buffer live: heaps and memory types, vertex and index buffers, three ways to upload data into VRAM, and allocators that place thousands of resources in a few blocks.

lessons.title: Memory heaps and memory types
lessons.summary: A buffer and its memory are two objects: the heaps and types a GPU reports, memory requirements and memoryTypeBits, and the rule that picks a type.

lessons.title: Vertex and index buffers
lessons.summary: Vertices from memory instead of shader constants: bindings, attributes and Slang locations, an index buffer that stores each vertex once, and the simplest placement in mappable memory.

lessons.title: Staging uploads
lessons.summary: Three ways into VRAM - a copy on the graphics queue, a copy on the transfer queue with an ownership transfer, a direct write through the BAR window - with measured costs, and why a fence does not make a copy visible.

lessons.title: Allocators and sub-allocation
lessons.summary: Why real programs make a few big allocations and place thousands of resources inside them: the measured cost of vkAllocateMemory, alignment rules, a linear allocator in Rust and VMA in C++.

modules.title: Descriptors and shader data
modules.summary: How shaders get data that is not a vertex: uniform buffers and their layout rules, descriptor sets, push constants and push descriptors, GPU pointers, and one bindless table for everything.

lessons.title: Uniform buffers
lessons.summary: Per-frame data in a uniform buffer per frame in flight, written through a persistent mapping, and the std140, std430 and scalar layout rules checked against the SPIR-V.

lessons.title: Descriptor sets
lessons.summary: Set layout, pool, set, update, bind: how set 0, binding 0 in a shader becomes a real buffer, when a set may change, and why sets are grouped by how often they change.

lessons.title: Push constants and push descriptors
lessons.summary: Bytes or a descriptor recorded straight into the command buffer: 256 bytes guaranteed in Vulkan 1.4, push descriptors in core 1.4, and the three roads compared.

lessons.title: Buffer device address
lessons.summary: 64-bit GPU pointers instead of descriptors: the feature and the flags they require, pointers in Slang, and GPU-assisted validation catching a read past the end.

lessons.title: Bindless descriptors
lessons.summary: One set with a big descriptor array, bound once and indexed per instance: descriptor indexing, the four binding flags, updates while frames are in flight, and non-uniform indexing.

modules.title: Images
modules.summary: Images the GPU reads, tests and averages: textures with samplers, depth buffers and Vulkan's clip space, mip chains generated with blits, and multisample anti-aliasing with a resolve.

lessons.title: Textures and samplers
lessons.summary: From CPU pixels to Sampler2D.Sample: optimal tiling, format features, a staging copy into an image with two layout transitions, the image view, the sampler, and why color textures are _SRGB.

lessons.title: Depth buffers
lessons.summary: A per-pixel depth test instead of draw order: choosing a depth format, the depth attachment, test and write, Vulkan clip space and where the projection's precision goes, and the barrier a shared depth image needs.

lessons.title: Mipmaps
lessons.summary: Why a far floor shimmers: the mip chain and its memory, generating it with vkCmdBlitImage2 and a barrier per level, how the sampler picks a level, and anisotropic filtering.

lessons.title: Multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA)
lessons.summary: Smooth edges without shading every sample: supported sample counts, multisampled transient attachments, the resolve at the end of a rendering, the memory it costs and what MSAA does not fix.

modules.title: Compute
modules.summary: The GPU without triangles: compute pipelines, workgroups and dispatches, shared memory and workgroup barriers, a particle system that compute writes and graphics draws, and async compute on a queue of its own, measured.

lessons.title: Compute pipelines
lessons.summary: A one-stage pipeline and a grid of workgroups: choosing the workgroup size, ceil-division and the bounds check, storage buffers, a groupshared reduction with workgroup barriers, and reading results back through HOST_CACHED memory.

lessons.title: Particles
lessons.summary: A million particles in one buffer that a compute shader moves and the draw reads as points: the barriers within a frame and across frames in flight, and why one buffer is enough when the CPU never touches it.

lessons.title: Async compute
lessons.summary: The simulation on a compute-only queue: ping-pong buffers, two timeline semaphores and the wait validation missed, CONCURRENT versus EXCLUSIVE, timestamps across queues, and why it gains nothing measurable on the course GPU.

modules.title: Advanced
modules.summary: Tools and techniques beyond the basic frame, starting with debugging and profiling from inside the program: what it can tell the validation layer and the tools, and what the GPU can measure about its own work.

lessons.title: Debugging and profiling
lessons.summary: Object names and labels the validation layer and the tools quote, printf from a shader, query pools with timestamps and pipeline statistics, calibrated timestamps that put GPU work on the CPU's clock, and where RenderDoc and Nsight take over.

labs.title: Warp divergence
labs.summary: 32 lanes, one instruction stream: write a condition and watch the warp run both branches with lanes switched off.

labs.title: Where the data lives
labs.summary: VRAM, system RAM and the PCIe bus between them, with the real bandwidths of the course GPU: what a frame costs if a buffer crosses the bus.

labs.title: The path of a command
labs.summary: CPU records, submits, moves on; the GPU runs the work later. A CPU/GPU timeline you can scrub.

labs.title: OpenGL state vs Vulkan pipelines
labs.summary: Change state in a GL-style driver and see when it has to rebuild a shader behind your back; do the same with prebuilt Vulkan pipelines.

labs.title: Through the loader
labs.summary: Pick a Vulkan call and the enabled layers, then follow it from the trampoline through the layers to the terminator and the drivers.

labs.title: Debug messenger filters
labs.summary: Severity and type masks applied to a real validation log: which messages reach your callback.

labs.title: Pick a GPU
labs.summary: The real properties, features and limits of the course GPU, and the picking rule of step 03 that you can change.

labs.title: Queue planner
labs.summary: The real queue families of the course GPU: choose graphics, async compute and transfer queues and see what you get.

labs.title: Build the object tree
labs.summary: Create and destroy Vulkan objects in any order; the simulator answers with the real validation rules.

labs.title: Queues, semaphores and fences
labs.summary: Submit batches to several queues with wait and signal semaphores and a fence: see what overlaps, what waits and where a race appears.

labs.title: Assemble the frame loop
labs.summary: Two frames in flight, step by step: wait, acquire, reset, record, submit, present. Wrong steps are refused with the real validation rule or a labeled deadlock or hazard.

labs.title: Write the barriers
labs.summary: Seven short command streams, most from the course steps, with eight empty barriers to write where commands touch the same memory: choose stage masks, access masks and layouts. Invalid structs are refused with the real VUID, open hazards are reported, correct barriers graded tight or wider than needed.

labs.title: The graphics pipeline
labs.summary: Walk the stages from vertex input to color output, and see which state is baked into a pipeline and which is dynamic in Vulkan 1.4.

labs.title: Buffers and memory
labs.summary: From buffer usage to memory requirements to a memory type of the real course GPU, and a staging upload or a direct write through the BAR window.
